pages.title: The People of Gensokyo
pages.text: Gensokyo is home to many characters: the shrine maiden at the Hakurei Shrine, the ordinary magician in the forest, the shopkeeper at Kourindou, and more. They keep to places all over the world.$(br2)You can build a bond with them: a gift they like, a hearty feast, a finished errand — each raises your $(bold)reputation$(). Reputation is shown when you talk to them; the higher it is, the more they will trade and the more quests they will unlock.

$(bold)Talking$()$(br)Right-click a character to talk. Some topics only appear once you are close enough, or once some other condition is met. Right-clicking with a gift item instead gives it to her: how much reputation it earns depends on her taste, and an item she has no liking for is not taken.$(br2)After receiving a gift she likes, she will give you something back in your next conversation.

$(bold)Requests$()$(br)Quests come in daily and one-time kinds. Each one lists what it needs and what it pays.$(br2)Finishing key quests also raises the ceiling on the reputation you can build; gifts and hospitality alone will not get you there.

$(bold)Their Homes$()$(br)A major character has a home of her own, and her bed is the heart of it and her anchor — even if she is knocked out or dies by accident, she will respawn at the bed before long, so never break or move it. If you cannot find her, look around her house; she keeps close to it. See $(l:decoration/character_beds)Character Beds$(/l).$(br2)Characters keep to their homes, so carrying one off will not work; a broken bed makes the whole structure stop working and loses the bed's data. Now and then a character will visit another's home during the day. A visitor has no bed there and offers no quests, but she will still talk, trade, and accept a finished quest.
